name: floating-stack
title: Floating stack
description: A corner for floating widgets that do not collide: back to top, a chat launcher and a feedback tab stack with safe gaps.
docs: The children are your widgets, the first one nearest the corner. corner is bottom-end (the default), bottom-start, top-end or top-start; end and start follow the writing direction. gap is sm, md, lg or a length; offset is the distance from the edges in pixels or any CSS length, 20 by default, with the safe-area insets added. The stack ignores pointer events and only its children receive them, it hides in print, and the document order equals the visual order from the corner, so Tab reaches the widget in the corner first. respectChrome lifts a bottom stack above a fixed bottom bar or the on-screen keyboard, whichever reaches higher (the keyboard covers the bar and the home indicator, so the two are never added up), and drops a top stack under a fixed header: it reads --chrome-bottom and --chrome-top, which ChromeOffsets publishes, and measures the keyboard through the visual viewport (keyboardInset replaces the measurement). label names the group for assistive technology.
